title: How Google DeepMind Runs Agents at Scale — KP Sawhney & Ian Ballantyne, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: The talk is a panel/demo about DeepMind's internal agent harness, Antigravity, and scaling concerns rather than a detailed architecture. Actionable mechanisms are quota-aware model mixing/fallback, mock-compute evals, shared-file collaboration, specialized auto-review, trajectory observability, and curated skills.

takeaways.technique: Tiered model mix with quota-aware fallback
takeaways.what_they_do: They mix free/local models for bulk work with advanced models only for specific agentic components, and expect seamless fallback when a model quota is exhausted so the workflow does not stall.
takeaways.evidence_quote: mixing and matching between models like Gemma 4 which which are effectively free from a quota perspective

takeaways.what_they_do: They use mock TPUs to test the harness and agentic flow without consuming real TPU hours, separating harness correctness from model/compute cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: mock TPUs so that, you know, you can test the harness itself and and the agentic flow, but not necessarily using up a ton of uh, TPU hours

takeaways.technique: Shared workspace instead of giant context blobs
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of passing huge text blobs through a pipeline, they want pipeline stages to collaborate through a shared file system, like human researchers sharing artifacts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: why not have the different parts of that pipeline collaborate in in a shared file system

takeaways.what_they_do: They use a language-specific auto-review model fine-tuned on style guides and good examples, plus product-specific review prompts/SRIs to improve reviewer signal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: on a per language basis, we have a specific like auto review model that has been um fine-tuned on all of our style guides

takeaways.technique: Agent trajectory store for loop diagnosis
takeaways.what_they_do: They keep an agent trajectory store and custom observability UI to drill into steps and raw model requests, specifically to find where looping or off-rails behavior began.
takeaways.evidence_quote: diagnose at what exact point looping started happening or you know, the model went off the rails

takeaways.what_they_do: They build a large internal skills library but focus on improving skills and letting only the best survive, to avoid uncontrolled skill sprawl.
takeaways.evidence_quote: making sure that only the best ones uh survive really, almost Darwinian nature
